prerequisites: Knowledge for calculating state changes of ideal gases

learning_outcomes.text: Students are able to analyze and interpret thermodynamic processes and state changes of different substances using state diagrams and calculations.
Students can describe the behavior of real gases and differentiate them from ideal gases, and apply the equations of state for real gases.
Students understand the thermodynamic states and state changes of pure fluids and can represent and analyze them in state diagrams.
Students can describe, calculate, and energetically evaluate right-running cyclic processes such as the Clausius-Rankine process.
Students are able to explain measures for increasing the efficiency of cyclic processes and analyze their technical implementation.
Students understand the functioning of left-running cyclic processes, as used in refrigeration machines and heat pumps, and can design and evaluate them.
Students know the thermodynamic properties of moist air, can analyze its states and processes, and apply them to technical applications such as air conditioning systems.
Students can describe the states and state changes of two-component mixtures and analyze their thermodynamic behavior.
Students understand the concepts of exergy and anergy, can set up exergy balances, and use them for evaluating thermodynamic processes.

syllabus_topics: States and state changes of pure fluids
Right-running cyclic processes of pure fluids (e.g., Clausius-Rankine process)
Measures for increasing the efficiency of cyclic processes
Left-running cyclic processes for refrigeration machines and heat pumps
Thermodynamics of moist air (states and processes)
Thermodynamics of mixtures (states and state changes of two-component mixtures)
Concepts of exergy and anergy; exergy balances
assessment_rules: Credit points are awarded upon successful completion of the module examination.
